results.title: Prime counting in a residue class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $X$, $q$ and $a$, $\pi(X; q, a)$ is the number of primes $p \le X$ with $p \equiv a \pmod q$. The modulus $q = 1$ is allowed, and for $q = 0$ the congruence means $p = a$.

results.title: Prime counting modulo one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $X$ and $a$, the number $\pi(X; 1, a)$ of primes $p \le X$ with $p \equiv a \pmod 1$ equals $\pi(X)$, the number of primes $p \le X$.

results.title: Residue-class prime count as a filtered range
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$, $q$ and $a$, the number $\pi(n; q, a)$ of primes $p \le n$ with $p \equiv a \pmod q$ equals the number of integers $p$ with $0 \le p \le n$ such that $p$ is prime and $p \equiv a \pmod q$.

results.title: Chebyshev's function in a residue class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $q$, a residue class $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ and a real number $x$, $\psi(x; q, a)$ is the sum of the von Mangoldt function $\Lambda(n)$ over the positive integers $n \le x$ with $n \equiv a \pmod q$.

results.title: The residue-class Chebyshev function vanishes below one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $q$, every residue class $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ and every real number $x < 1$, we have $\psi(x; q, a) = 0$, where $\psi(x; q, a)$ is the sum of the von Mangoldt function $\Lambda(n)$ over the positive integers $n \le x$ with $n \equiv a \pmod q$.

results.title: Prime number theorem for Chebyshev's function in a reduced residue class
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $q \ge 1$ be an integer, let $b$ be a unit of $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$, let $\Lambda$ be the von Mangoldt function and let $\varphi$ be Euler's totient function. For real $x$ let $\psi(x; q, b)$ be the sum of $\Lambda(n)$ over the integers $1 \le n \le x$ with $n \equiv b \pmod{q}$. Then $\psi(x; q, b)/x \to 1/\varphi(q)$ as the real number $x$ tends to infinity.

results.title: Prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $q \ge 2$ and $a$ be natural numbers with $\gcd(a, q) = 1$, and for each natural number $n$ let $N(n)$ be the number of primes $p \le n$ with $p \equiv a \pmod q$. Then $N(n) \log n / n \to 1 / \varphi(q)$ as $n \to \infty$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function and $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

results.title: Prime number theorem for the residue-class prime count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $q \ge 2$ and $a$ be natural numbers with $\gcd(a, q) = 1$, and let $\pi(n; q, a)$ be the number of primes $p \le n$ with $p \equiv a \pmod q$. Then $\pi(n; q, a) \log n / n \to 1 / \varphi(q)$ as $n \to \infty$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function and $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

results.title: Primitive pseudoperfect numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ lies in $A$, the set of primitive pseudoperfect numbers, when $n > 0$, $n$ is pseudoperfect (it is positive and equal to the sum of some set of distinct proper divisors of itself), and no proper divisor of $n$ (a divisor $m \mid n$ with $m < n$) is pseudoperfect.

results.title: Erdős Problem 469 (statement)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that the reciprocals of the primitive pseudoperfect numbers have finite sum: the family $(1/n)$, indexed by the natural numbers $n$ that are primitive pseudoperfect, is summable in $\mathbb{R}$. Here $n$ is pseudoperfect if $n > 0$ and $n$ is the sum of some set of distinct proper divisors of $n$, and primitive pseudoperfect if moreover no proper divisor of $n$ is pseudoperfect.

results.title: Reciprocals of primitive pseudoperfect numbers have finite sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Call a natural number $n$ pseudoperfect if $n > 0$ and $n$ is the sum of some set of distinct proper divisors of $n$, and primitive pseudoperfect if moreover no proper divisor of $n$ is pseudoperfect. Then the family $(1/n)$, indexed by the primitive pseudoperfect numbers $n$, is summable in $\mathbb{R}$, that is, the sum of $1/n$ over all primitive pseudoperfect numbers $n$ is finite.

results.title: Erdős Problem 825
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Write $\sigma(n)$ for the sum of the positive divisors of a positive integer $n$, and call $n$ pseudoperfect if $n$ is the sum of the elements of some set of proper divisors of $n$. The statement is the conjunction of two claims: there is a real $C > 0$ such that every positive integer $n$ with $\sigma(n) > Cn$ is pseudoperfect, and every real $C > 0$ with this property satisfies $C > 2$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 825 is true
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $\sigma(n)$ for the sum of the positive divisors of a positive integer $n$, and call $n$ pseudoperfect if $n$ is the sum of the elements of some set of proper divisors of $n$. Then there is a real $C > 0$ such that every positive integer $n$ with $\sigma(n) > Cn$ is pseudoperfect, and every real $C > 0$ with this property satisfies $C > 2$.

results.title: Recurrence for the alternating stride sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $q \ge 1$, $n \ge 1$ and $t \ge 0$ be integers and let $S_{q,t}$ denote the alternating stride sum. Then $S_{q,t}(n + q) = 1/(n + q)^t - S_{q,t}(n)$.

results.title: Terms of the Gauss–Kuzmin–Wirsing series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, a real number $x$ and a natural number $k$, the $k$-th term of the Gauss–Kuzmin–Wirsing series of $f$ at $x$ is $\frac{1}{(x+k+1)^2} f\left(\frac{1}{x+k+1}\right)$, with the convention $1/0 = 0$.

results.title: The Gauss–Kuzmin–Wirsing operator has eigenvalue one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that is continuous on $[0, 1]$, bounded on $[0, 1]$ and not identically zero on $[0, 1]$, such that $\sum_{k \ge 1} \frac{1}{(x+k)^2} f\left(\frac{1}{x+k}\right) = f(x)$ for every $x \in [0, 1]$; that is, $1$ is an eigenvalue of the Gauss–Kuzmin–Wirsing operator in the continuous model.

results.title: Terms of the complex Gauss–Kuzmin–Wirsing series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, a complex number $z$ and a natural number $k$, the $k$-th term of the Gauss–Kuzmin–Wirsing series of $f$ at $z$ is $\frac{1}{(z+k+1)^2} f\left(\frac{1}{z+k+1}\right)$, with the convention $1/0 = 0$.

results.title: Wirsing constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Wirsing constant is the supremum in $\mathbb{R}$ of $|\lambda|$ over all holomorphic eigenvalues $\lambda \ne 1$ of the Gauss–Kuzmin–Wirsing operator on the Mayer disk $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z - 1| < 3/2\}$, with the convention that the supremum is $0$ when there is no such $\lambda$ or when these absolute values are unbounded.
